chunks: From him, from Ibn Jabalah, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The salat in residence is eight rakʿahs when the sun declines, in the time between that and when two-thirds of the qāmah has passed. Then when two-thirds of the qāmah has passed, you begin with the obligatory prayer.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the salat being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.ثَمَانِي رَكَعَاتٍ: eight rakʿahs performed in this time period
key_terms.ثُلُثَا الْقَامَةِ: two-thirds of a qāmah, a measure used here for determining time
key_terms.زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: the sun declined from the meridian, marking the start of the time

ai.seo_question: When does one begin the obligatory zuhr salat after the sun declines according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling about the time of the noon prayer in residence and the performance of eight rakʿahs before the obligatory prayer after the sun’s decline. It indicates that these rakʿahs are performed until the passing of two-thirds of a qāmah, after which one begins the obligatory salat.
